content:
## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `cmp32` (32-bit registered unsigned comparator: y = (a < b)) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module cmp32 (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire valid_i,
    input wire [31:0] a_i,
    input wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg valid_o,
    output reg [0:0] y_o
);

wire lt_0 = (a_i[31:0] < b_i[31:0]);
wire eq_0 = (a_i[31:0] == b_i[31:0]);

wire cmp_0 = lt_0;

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o <= 1'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;
        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= cmp_0;
    end
end
endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 268.926 um^2, WNS 7.62112 ns, score 75.942274.
estimate_ppa on this RTL returns area 177.156 um^2, WNS 7.69083 ns, estimated score 76.731144 (estimates omit tap cells, buffering and wiring, so compare estimates with estimates).

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: simulate, prove_equivalence, estimate_ppa, place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

content.text: I'll start by testing a cleaned-up version of the RTL (removing dead code) with the cheap estimation tools before committing to a place_and_route run.

All estimated variants (dead-code removal, ripple-borrow chain, explicit Sklansky tree, subtractor-based) either matched or underperformed the original specification's default `<` synthesis in estimated reward. The original RTL (after trivial dead-code removal, which Yosys already does automatically) remains the best candidate. Let's confirm functional correctness and run the full place-and-route flow on it.

content.text: The baseline matches exactly as expected. Let's test the ripple-borrow variant with full place-and-route, since its area estimate was notably lower (131 vs 177) despite a small WNS penalty — the actual post-route numbers (with buffering/routing) could differ from the pre-placement estimate.

All three alternative implementations (dead-code-removed baseline, ripple-borrow chain, Sklansky tree) were tested. The full place-and-route results show the original specification's default `<` synthesis (score 75.942274) is the best of the tested variants — both the ripple-borrow and tree restructurings reduced area somewhat but incurred a larger relative WNS penalty (which is weighted 10x more heavily than area in the score), yielding worse final scores. I'll stop here and keep the baseline result as the best verified submission.

input.summary: Explored several equivalent RTL restructurings of the 32-bit unsigned comparator (plain dead-code-cleaned baseline, an explicit ripple-borrow chain, an explicit Sklansky-style balanced compare/equal reduction tree, and a subtractor-based sign-bit approach), verifying functional equivalence with simulate/prove_equivalence and screening with estimate_ppa before spending place_and_route budget. All alternative structures reduced pre-route area but also slightly reduced WNS, and because the score weights WNS 10x more than area (score = 10*WNS - 0.001*area), every restructuring underperformed the original specification's default '<' synthesis after full place-and-route: baseline gave area 268.926 um^2, WNS 7.62112 ns, score 75.942274; ripple-borrow gave area 223.174, WNS 7.60301, score 75.806926; the balanced tree gave area 262.01, WNS 7.61287, score 75.86669. The original specification (whose logic Yosys/ABC already reduces to essentially the same optimized network regardless of superficial RTL rewrites) remains the best verified result, so it is kept as the final answer.
